From 4ae1709a314060a196981b344610d023ea841e57 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sven Eckelmann <sven@narfation.org>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 22:20:50 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] batman-adv: bla: prevent use-after-free when deleting claims

When batadv_bla_del_backbone_claims() removes all claims for a backbone, it
does this by dropping the link entry in the hash list. This list entry
itself was one of the references which need to be dropped at the same time
via batadv_claim_put().

But the batadv_claim_put() must not be done before the last access to the
claim object in this function. Otherwise the claim might be freed already
by the batadv_claim_release() function before the list entry was dropped.

Cc: stable@kernel.org
Fixes: 23721387c409 ("batman-adv: add basic bridge loop avoidance code")
Signed-off-by: Sven Eckelmann <sven@narfation.org>

diff --git a/net/batman-adv/bridge_loop_avoidance.c b/net/batman-adv/bridge_loop_avoidance.c
index 51fe028b9088..8b77dd2ecfa4 100644
--- a/net/batman-adv/bridge_loop_avoidance.c
+++ b/net/batman-adv/bridge_loop_avoidance.c
@@ -318,8 +318,8 @@ batadv_bla_del_backbone_claims(struct batadv_bla_backbone_gw *backbone_gw)
 			if (claim->backbone_gw != backbone_gw)
 				continue;
 
-			batadv_claim_put(claim);
 			hlist_del_rcu(&claim->hash_entry);
+			batadv_claim_put(claim);
 		}
 		spin_unlock_bh(list_lock);
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

**Modifications in each file:**

- **`net/batman-adv/bridge_loop_avoidance.c`**: In `batadv_bla_del_backbone_claims()`, the order of two operations was swapped. Previously, `batadv_claim_put(claim)` was called before `hlist_del_rcu(&claim->hash_entry)`. The patch moves `batadv_claim_put(claim)` after the `hlist_del_rcu()` call.

**Relationship between changes:**

The single change directly addresses a use-after-free bug. The `batadv_claim_put()` function may decrement the reference count of the claim; if it reaches zero, `batadv_claim_release()` frees the claim object. Calling it before `hlist_del_rcu()` leaves a window where the claim can be freed while it is still linked in the hash list. The subsequent `hlist_del_rcu()` would then access freed memory. By swapping the order, the claim is safely removed from the hash list first, and only then is the reference put, preventing any use-after-free. The fix ensures that all accesses to the claim (specifically the `hash_entry` field) occur while the claim is still valid.
